summary:
Our hull looks like a robot mainly because every edge in it is sharp. I measured R = 0 at the deck edge (sheer), the coachroof roof edge, the coachroof front, both coaming top edges, the transom top, the transom/side corner and the stem. Bambu softens all of these by about the same amount, R ≈ 20-26 mm full scale (0.7-0.9 mm on the model). It also runs soft beads along the lines: a toe rail of 32 × 18 mm and a strake of about 56 × 16 mm. In flat shading those beads give the thin highlight lines that read as 'fine lines'.

Several boxy parts make it worse:
- **Coachroof front:** it is a vertical wall. The 45° cut in deckhouse.py:200 silently removes nothing (the volume is the same before and after), even though the README says the front is a 45° face.
- **Anchor-roller block:** a 520 × 170 mm brick. Below the deck it sticks out 107 mm ahead of the raked stem.
- **Rubbing strake:** a square 95 × 55 mm bar with a flat cut-off end at the bow. Going round the transom corner it has kinks of 16°, 10° and 26°.
- **Sprayhood:** a loaf with flat vertical ends. It swallows the Ø300 winch drums, which poke out of its sides.
- **Cleats:** flat-topped bricks, 260 × 90 × 100 mm.

I tested fillets in a scratch copy of the code. Rounding the hull deck edge (R25) fails, rounding the transom edges (R10 and R20) fails, and rounding the coachroof roof edge (R25) gives an invalid solid. Rounding the top of the cockpit coaming (R25) works. So the radii have to be built into the section and profile shapes; only simple stand-alone blocks can be filleted.

Suggested radii are 20-30 mm full scale (0.7-1.0 mm model). That is 3-5 layer steps at 0.2 mm, so it shows on the print and not just on screen. Radii under about 9 mm full scale (0.3 mm model) disappear in print.

Order by payoff per effort:
1. Fix the coachroof front.
2. Shrink the anchor roller and clip it to the deck.
3. Give the strake a rounded profile and finer path points.
4. Build a radius into the deck edge of the hull sections.
5. Round the coachroof roof edge in its profile.
6. Reshape the ends of the sprayhood and move the winches out of it.
7. Make cleats and winches smaller.
8. Fillet the coaming top.
9. Round the stem and the bow tip.
10. Transom edges (hard to do).
11. Keel root (KEEL_FILLET is defined but never used).

Method note: the STL sits on the plate at 45°, not 44°. With -44° the mast hole lands 25 mm off the centreline. All measurements here use -45°.

findings.title: Coachroof front is a vertical wall: the 45-degree step-wedge cut silently does nothing
findings.claim: The sloped front the drawing shows (about 48 deg, from x=2197 at the deck to 2322 at the roof; the README says 45 deg) is missing from the STL. Instead there is a vertical wall at x=2200, 135-150 mm high (4.5-5 mm model), with a sharp top edge. The cause is that prism.intersect(roof).cut(_step_wedge()) returns the coachroof uncut. OCC fails silently here: the slope of the wedge starts exactly at the tip vertex (2200, 0) of the planform. robust_cut only checks the number of solids, and this cut is not even routed through it.
findings.evidence: Centreline section of the STL: the front face is at x=2198-2200 from z=1217 to 1351, with a 91.0 deg corner and a corner-cut distance of 0.0 mm (R=0). The plan section at z=1300 starts at x=2201; with the slope it would start at about 2291. I rebuilt the coachroof in a scratch copy: its volume is 3.1835e9 mm3 before and after the cut, and prism∩roof∩wedge = 0. Translating the wedge by +-0.37, +-1 or +5 mm makes the cut work and removes 2.4-3.0 L. The README's own overlay (overlegg-profil.jpg) shows the red vertical front standing over the drawn slope. Bambu's front is 78 deg with a top edge of R≈25 mm (0.83 mm model).
findings.where: hr26/deckhouse.py:174-187 (_step_wedge), :200 (cut); hr26/params.py:134-135 (STEP_X0/X1); hr26/build.py:64-69 (robust_cut has no volume check); README 'Videre arbeid'
findings.fix: Smallest fix: nudge the wedge, for example .translate((-0.37,0,0)) or start the slope at STEP_X0-0.5. Robust fix: build the slope into the roof profile so no boolean is needed. Let roof_z(x) run from the deck at 2200 to the roof at 2330, with rounded transitions of R 40-60 mm full (1.3-2 mm model) at the roof edge, matching 'the original is rounded'. Then _roof_body produces the front directly. Also add a check to robust_cut and coachroof() that raises if |dV| < 1 mm3.
findings.risk: low; this restores the measured drawing line. Check that the forehatch at 2490 still sits on the roof.

findings.title: Anchor-roller block: oversized brick that pokes out of the raked stem
findings.claim: anchor_roller() is a 520 x 170 mm block running from 420 mm below the deck to 140 mm above it, at x=170-690, with R60 on its vertical edges only. Above the deck that is a 17.3 x 5.7 x 4.7 mm brick on the model. Below the deck its flat front at x=170 sits ahead of the stem from z=793 to 947: the stem crosses z=793 at x=277. So a box corner 107 mm long (3.6 mm model) and 154 mm tall (5.1 mm) hangs out under the stem head and out of the narrow bow flanks. Its underside is an unsupported flat overhang of 3.6 mm.
findings.evidence: Centreline section of the STL: block front at x=170 from z=793 to 1353; the lofted stem is at x=277 (z=793), 202 (z=900) and 135 (z=1000), matching the analytic stem within 4 mm. The plan section at z=1300 shows a loop of 520 x 170 centred at x=430, y=0. In the overlay crop, the red block sits ahead of the drawn stem line, and the drawing has no tall block on the foredeck. Bambu has no block; a rounded rim wraps round the stem (see edges_closeups.png and edges_vs_drawing.png).
findings.fix: Start the block at deck level (offset z-20 instead of z-420), or intersect it with the hull envelope, so it can never leave the stem. Shrink it to about 300 x 100 mm and 50-60 mm high (10 x 3.3 x 2 mm model). Round the top edges by R≈30 mm (1 mm model); a fillet on the stand-alone block before the union is safe, as the coaming test shows. If photos confirm it, add a small roller lug at the stem head. The drawing shows the strake line ending in a small fitting about 100 mm ahead of the stem.

findings.title: Rubbing strake: square bar, flat cut-off bow end, faceted path and a knuckle round the stern corner
findings.claim: The strake is a ruled loft through 95 x 110 rectangles, half buried so it stands 55 mm proud. That gives 4 sharp longitudinal edges (R=0) and a flat underside overhang of 1.8 mm (model) that droops in print. At x=200 it ends in a flat 95 x 55 face (3.2 x 1.8 mm model). The path has 53 points per side: along the side, segments of 210-270 mm with kinks of 0.9-2.5 deg (median 1.2 deg); round the stern corner (x 7635-7841) only 3 facets with kinks of 16.0, 10.4 and 26.0 deg, which form a visible knuckle. Bambu's strake is a soft bead about 56 mm high and 16 mm proud with crown R≈38 mm, running continuously round the transom.
findings.evidence: STL section at x=3200 shows the rectangle with square corners (edges_sections.png). I evaluated _strake_path(48) from the code: 53 points; kinks as listed; the side-to-transom turn is 52 deg over 206 mm. The close-ups (edges_details.png) show the flat bow end and the stern knuckle. The side kinks have a sagitta of 260 x 0.035/8 ≈ 1.1 mm full scale (0.04 mm model), so they are screen-only; the knuckle, the flat end and the square profile show in print.
findings.where: hr26/hull.py:104-140 (_strake_path; stations(48) at :122, 12 transom points at :135), :170-173 (4-corner polygon, ruled=True); hr26/params.py:235-237
findings.fix: Use a rounded D or half-ellipse profile of 12-16 points per station, for example 70 mm high x 30-35 mm proud with R 15-17 mm corners (0.5-0.6 mm model). Alternatively give it a 45-deg chamfered underside, which prints without support. Densify the path round the stern corner (10 or more points following the measured STERN_OUTLINE corner) and along the side (about 100 stations, or ruled=False). Taper the profile to zero over the last 150-200 mm at the bow, or run it to the stem fitting as the drawing does. All of this is built into the profile, which is robust; keep it half buried so the union still works.
findings.risk: low; a ruled loft of polygons is robust. With more points, check that the union with the hull still gives one solid (NUDGES).

findings.title: Sharp deck edge (sheer crease) along the whole hull; OCC fillet fails, so build the radius into the section wire
findings.claim: _section_wire joins the topside spline and the deck-arc spline with no tangency, so the whole sheer is a crease. At x=3200 the interior angle is 75.4 deg and the corner-cut distance is 0.3 mm, so R≈0. Bambu's deck edge has R≈22 mm (0.72 mm model) plus a toe-rail bead 32 x 18 mm with crown R 15 mm. The sheer is the most important line on a boat, and it currently has no highlight.
findings.evidence: STL section at x=3200: corner at y=1132, z=1143; the 3-point radius test sits at the floor value for a sharp corner (3.1 mm at +-5 mm). Bambu at x=3200: corner-cut R 21.7 mm and the toe-rail circle fit described above. In a scratch copy, fillet(25) on the 2 sheer edges of the bare hull_solid(40,26) gives StdFail_NotDone.
findings.fix: Insert a tangent arc of R≈25 mm full scale (0.83 mm model, about 4 layer steps) at each station's deck-edge corner. Trim both the side and the deck arc by R/tan(a/2) ≈ 32 mm, then add 4-6 arc points (or one extra spline edge). The measured sheer and deck outline remain the virtual intersection. The outermost point moves 32 mm down the side and about 7 mm inboard, so beam drops by about 14 mm (-0.5%) unless the virtual corner is pushed out 7 mm. Update section_inner/deck_arc_inner and keep the wall at 45 mm. As an option, add a separate rounded toe-rail bead, but only if photos show one.
findings.risk: medium; touches every station wire and the shell offset. Loft stability near the bow (tiny sections) and the transom cut need a re-check.

findings.title: Coachroof: vertical walls and a sharp roof edge; OCC fillet gives an invalid solid
findings.claim: The coachroof is a plan prism intersected with the roof body, which gives vertical walls and a roof edge of 91.7 deg with a corner cut of 1.6 mm, R≈4 mm (0.14 mm model). That vanishes in print, so the edge is effectively sharp. Bambu's roof edge has R≈23 mm (0.78 mm model) and its sides lean in 12.6 deg.
findings.evidence: STL section at x=3200: corner at y=922, z=1354. Bambu at x=3200: corner-cut R 23.5 mm; its side runs from y=676 at z=1290 to y=638 at z=1460. Scratch test after fixing the wedge: faces('>Z').edges().fillet(25) returns isValid()=False (dV 3.77 L), and fillet(40) gives StdFail_NotDone.
findings.fix: Build the radius into the roof body. Give each _roof_body section shoulders: the camber arc out to ±(w(x)-R), then a quarter-round down past the wall at w(x)=coach_half_width(x), with R≈25-30 mm (0.8-1.0 mm model). Alternatively loft the coachroof directly from rounded-rectangle sections. Lean the sides 8-12 deg inward only if photos confirm it; the deck plan only fixes the outline at one level.
findings.risk: low-medium; at the rounded front (plan R700) the x-sections cut the edge obliquely, so the radius grows slightly there.

findings.title: Sprayhood is a loaf with flat vertical ends, about 170 mm too long aft, and it swallows the winch drums
findings.claim: The sprayhood loft runs through 11 arch sections from 5135 to 6150 and ends in flat vertical faces at both ends with R=0 edges. The drawing shows a raked front and a rounded aft hoop. The winch drums at x=5900 (y≈880, D300) are inside the hood's length. Each drum's top (z≈1354) stands about 50 mm above the hood surface at the drum centre (z≈1306), so a cut cylinder pokes out of the flank like a funnel.
findings.evidence: STL centreline section: the front at x=5135 and the back at x=6150 stay constant from z=1450 to 1700, so both ends are vertical. Half-width at x=5600: 920 mm at z=1450 and 412 mm at z=1700; top at 1721-1745. The dashed hood in the drawing runs 5144-5978 at the top, its front rakes down to about 4880-4905, and its aft hoop foot is at about 6030 (edges_vs_drawing.png). Close-up: edges_details.png, bottom row. In Bambu the winches are small separate drums, not merged into the hood.
findings.fix: Add 2-3 end sections at each end that shrink the arch, so the loft ends in a small cap instead of a full flat face. Rake the front at about 45 deg, from the coachroof at about 4900 up to 5145. End the back hoop at about 5980 (top) to 6030 (foot), and round the top-back edge with R≈80-100 mm (2.7-3.3 mm model). Keep the hood inboard of the winches: narrow it to the coachroof width aft, or move WINCH_X aft of the hood.
findings.risk: low; a loft of arches is robust. Re-check that the cockpit cut still leaves the hood overhang and its print support.

findings.title: Cleats and winch drums are oversized flat-topped bricks and cans
findings.claim: There are 6 cleats, each a 260 x 90 mm block standing 100 mm above the deck, with R40 on the vertical edges and sharp top edges (8.7 x 3.0 x 3.3 mm model). The winch pads are cylinders of D300, 190 mm above the coaming top, with a 35 mm chamfer (Ø10 x 6.3 mm model). They are wider than the 130-mm coaming, so they overhang it on both sides. The stern cleat at x=7500 stands above every line of the profile drawing. The drawing gives no cleat size, so I cannot say what the real size is.
findings.evidence: STL plan section at z=1300: cleat loops 260 x 90 at x=700, y=±228 (hb-150); the top at z=1312 with the deck at about 1212. The fittings.py constants confirm the dimensions. The overlay crop at the stern shows the red cleat above the drawn lines. Bambu's deck hardware is small mushroom-shaped drums.
findings.fix: Make horn-style cleats: a low base plus two tapered horns, about 180 x 45 x 60 mm (6 x 1.5 x 2 mm model, printable with 3 perimeters). At minimum, use a 180 x 50 x 60 block with top edges R≈20 mm; a fillet on the stand-alone block before the union is safe. Make the winches about Ø150-180 x 150 with a domed top, reusing the vent recipe of fillet 0.4·D, which already works.

findings.title: Cockpit coaming: flat top with two sharp edges; here an OCC fillet works
findings.claim: The coaming is a plan prism (R200 corners in plan) intersected with a flat roof body (camber 0). Both top edges are R=0 (90.1 and 89.9 deg). The top is 130 mm wide (y 850-980) and stands 42 mm above the deck outboard. Bambu's inner top edge has R≈26 mm (0.86 mm model).
findings.evidence: STL section at x=6300: corners at (850, 1126) and (980, 1127) with a corner-cut distance of 0.0. Bambu at x=6300: corner-cut R 25.9 mm. In a scratch copy, D.coaming_block().faces('>Z').edges().fillet(25) gives a valid solid with dV -0.68 L.
findings.fix: Apply fillet(25) (0.83 mm model) to the top-face edges of the stand-alone coaming block before the union, inside try, and check the volume. Alternatively make the top a half-round with R≈60 mm.

findings.title: Knife-edge stem and a flat-capped bow tip
findings.claim: The bow sections start at y=0 and widen as y ∝ t^1.45, which has a horizontal tangent at the start, so the stem is a knife edge. The loft's first wire, at x=4, already has a deck half-breadth of 87 mm (the traced data gives 84.9 at x=0). The bow tip is therefore a flat planar cap 174 x 9 mm with two sharp corners in plan, where the plan drawing shows a rounded nose. Bambu's stem has R≈18-24 mm.
findings.evidence: 3-point radius test (±5 mm) on STL plan sections: 2.5 mm at z=1000 and 2.6 mm at z=1100. That is the floor value for a sharp V of about 40 deg. Bambu gives 24.1 mm at z=1100 and 17.9 mm at z=1200. The STL has 150 triangles in the plane x=4, spanning y ±87.2 and z 1197-1207. In the overlegg-plan.jpg crop, the red tip is a straight cut and the drawn nose is round, reaching about 26 mm further forward.
findings.where: hr26/curves.py:163-176 (the else branch and the t**1.45 ramp); hr26/hull.py:72-77 (first station at x=4); data/deck_halfbreadth.csv
findings.fix: Give the bow sections a square-root foot, y = sqrt(2·R·(x - x_stem(z))), blended into the existing ramp, with R≈20-25 mm (0.7-0.8 mm model). The stem line at y=0 stays on the measured profile. Close the deck outline with the round nose the drawing shows (about 36 mm long, ±85 mm wide) instead of the flat cap.
findings.risk: medium; it changes the bow waterlines within about 100 mm of the stem. Re-check the inner shell (VOID_BOW_EXTRA) and loft stability at the first stations.

findings.title: Transom edges are sharp, and OCC cannot fillet them in the current construction
findings.claim: The transom-to-deck edge is 94 deg with R=0. At z=600 the hull side turns about 30-45 deg onto the transom within 4 mm at x≈7825 (one vertex plus a sliver), so R≈0. Bambu's transom top has R≈20 mm (0.65 mm model), and its side corner has Rmin 26-53 mm.
findings.evidence: STL centreline section: corner at (7946, 958), angle 93.8 deg, corner-cut distance 0.0. Plan section at z=600: kinks of +40.8, -49.1 and -36.3 deg at x 7823-7827. Bambu: R 19.6 mm from the corner-cut fit; 3-point Rmin 26 mm (±5 mm) and 53 mm (±10 mm). In a scratch copy, fillet(10) and fillet(20) on the 3 transom-face edges of the bare hull_solid both give StdFail_NotDone.
findings.fix: Low priority. One option is a 15 mm (0.5 mm model) bevel, made by a second boolean with a cutter whose edge is offset along the transom boundary. Another is to post-process the STL locally near those edges. The deck outline already rounds the corner in plan (about R290); only the side-to-transom face edge is sharp.
findings.risk: high (OCC fillets fail; the workarounds add booleans on lofted B-spline faces)

findings.title: Keel root has no fillet although KEEL_FILLET = 90 is defined
findings.claim: params.py:80 defines KEEL_FILLET = 90.0 ('avrunding mot skroget', i.e. rounding against the hull), but no code uses it. The keel union leaves a sharp concave crease. It is visible when the model stands on its cradle. I cannot compare with Bambu, whose model has no keel.
findings.evidence: grep finds KEEL_FILLET only in params.py. STL section at x=4500: the keel side (y≈145 for z≤-500) meets the canoe body at z≈-490 within one 20-mm step (y=145 to 307).
findings.fix: Build the fillet into the keel loft: flare the top 1-2 keel sections, which already reach 260 mm up into the hull, so the foil widens by about 60-90 mm (2-3 mm model) towards the root. Do not use an OCC fillet on the union edge.

findings.title: Inventory of edge treatments in the code (task item 1); details that can stay as they are
findings.claim:
Each feature and its edge radius, full scale:
- Hull side/deck: crease, R0.
- Stem: knife edge, R0; flat 174 x 9 mm cap at x=4.
- Strake: rectangle, R0 on all 4 edges; flat ends.
- Transom (boolean cut): R0 to the deck, the sides and the bottom; name relief 10.5 mm (0.35 mm model), sharp.
- Coachroof: vertical walls; R0 at the roof edge and at the base; rounded only in plan (front R700, aft corners R140); the 45-deg front is missing (edges-1).
- Hatches: vertical corners R70, top chamfer 15 mm (0.5 mm model).
- Vents: top fillet 60 mm, so they are domes.
- Window recess: R55 corners in profile, 15 mm deep (0.5 mm model), sharp walls.
- Companionway: R60 on the edges along x, the rest R0; mostly hidden under the solid sprayhood.
- Sprayhood: rounded shoulders from 1-|a|^3.2; flat end faces with R0 edges.
- Cockpit well: vertical walls, R140 corners in plan, R0 top edges.
- Coaming: R200 in plan, flat top, R0 on both top edges.
- Winch pads: Ø300 with a 35 mm chamfer.
- Cleats: R40 on the vertical edges, R0 top edges.
- Anchor roller: R60 on the vertical edges, R0 top and bottom.
- Mast step: oval hole only, sharp rim; the separate 05_mastefot part covers it.
- Stanchion and pulpit holes: R0, which is fine.
- Keel root: R0.
Hatches, vents, the window recess and the name relief do not contribute to the robotic look: crisp window and hatch edges are realistic.
findings.evidence: Code: hull.py:21-40, 43-65, 143-174; deckhouse.py:96-118, 153-170, 203-251, 254-288, 311-335, 403-445; fittings.py:58-127, 156-185; params.py:80. The STL sections in edges_sections.png confirm R0 on every edge I measured.
findings.fix: No change needed for hatches, vents, window, name or holes. If anything, turn the hatch chamfer of 15 mm into a fillet of about 20 mm (0.67 mm model); the hatch top is a planar face, so this is safe.

findings.title: Method note: 01_skrog.stl sits on the plate at 45 deg, not 44 deg
findings.claim: Rotating the STL back by -44 deg leaves a 1-deg yaw. The y-extent minimum is flat between 44 and 46 deg, so it cannot decide the angle. With -45 deg every centred feature lands on y=0.
findings.evidence: At -44 deg: mast hole centre at y=-25 mm, anchor roller at y=-77 mm, port and starboard cleats 8 mm apart in x, and the roller measuring 521 x 177. At -45 deg: mast hole 135 x 105 at (3400, 0), roller 520 x 170 at (430, 0), cleats at y=±228 with x=700 on both sides. With -45 deg and the bow at x=4, the transom at z=300 is at 7850, against 7849.8 analytic, and the stem at z=1000 is at 135, against 134 analytic.
findings.where: hr26/build.py:143-151 (best_bed_angle, integer degrees); my lib.py ours_full()
findings.fix: Use -45 deg (or recompute from the symmetry of the mast hole) in all comparison scripts. Earlier overlays made with -44 deg carry about ±70 mm of yaw at the bow.
